- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing sudden price reversals or spikes — often underreacts to recent high volatility.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth, failing to reflect short-term volatility or sharp directional shifts in the last 7–10 days.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when true prices are rising.
- Model overreacts to recent low prices, producing overly pessimistic forecasts when prices are recovering.
- Model fails to account for mean reversion in the final 10–15 days — often forecasts higher prices than true outcomes after a sharp rise.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after a spike — tends to underestimate the depth of drawdowns or rebounds.
